entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Podemos (We Can), founded in January 2014 in Spain by Pablo Iglesias Turrión and a group of political scientists from the Complutense University of Madrid following the 15-M Indignados movement (2011), rose from 0 to 5 MEPs in four months, became Spain's third party in 2015 national elections, and entered government as a junior coalition partner with the PSOE (2020) — the first time a leftist coalition had governed Spain since the Second Republic (1931-1936). Podemos pioneered the 'discursive war' strategy: reframing politics as 'people vs. caste' rather than 'left vs. right'.

The 15-M Indignados movement (May 2011) — when hundreds of thousands occupied squares across Spain in protest against austerity, unemployment (25%, youth 50%), and political corruption — was Podemos's founding energy. Iglesias's 'Podemos' lecture at Complutense (January 2014) proposed a 'discourse machine': avoiding left-right framing in favor of 'democratic regeneration vs. the caste.' The January 2014 founding manifesto gathered 50,000 signatures in 24 hours.

Podemos's structural innovations: elected leadership through online voting (circulares), citizens' assemblies for policy, and deliberate use of TV talk shows (Iglesias became Spain's most famous political commentator before founding Podemos). The 2015 'Vistalegre I' assembly approved a more hierarchical structure; the 2020 coalition with PSOE (Pedro Sánchez) made Iglesias Vice President. Iglesias resigned in 2021 to run (unsuccessfully) for Madrid Community President; Yolanda Díaz succeeded him as Sumar leader, broadening the coalition.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Podemos — rising from 0 to government in six years using digital organization, discourse-machine strategy, and Indignados energy — achieved Spain's first leftist government since 1936 and pioneered the European left-populist political formula that inspired Syriza, LFI, and Corbynism.
